title: How To Have A Fun Classroom Without Extra Planning
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that classroom fun, in the sense that actually influences student behavior, doesn't require elaborate lessons, games, or incentive systems, and instead reframes it through students' own definition. He lays out eight facets of student-perceived fun: it's an attitude, a mood, a feeling of safety and comfort, a personal connection, something found in everyday absurd moments, storytelling, a deliberate choice to appreciate students, and something reciprocated by students who feel liked. He contrasts this low-effort, relational version of fun with time-consuming interactive activities, which he still endorses but frames as impractical to sustain minute by minute. The piece emphasizes that fun cannot be manufactured if a teacher doesn't genuinely like their students, since that authenticity is what makes the classroom connection real. He closes by tying this everyday sense of fun to stronger relationships, more leverage for the classroom management plan, and students' desire to please their teacher.
points: Redefine classroom fun through students' eyes: an attitude and mood rather than noise, games, or elaborate activities.
Rely on the minute-by-minute reality of genuine warmth and humor, since interactive lessons and games are too time-consuming to sustain daily.
Use storytelling deliberately; Linsin cites it as one of the most powerful tools for generating rapport and excitement in class.
Recognize fun as a choice tied to genuinely liking your students, especially difficult ones, since a grudge blocks the connection.
Expect reciprocity: students who feel liked and enjoy their classroom will work harder to please a teacher they appreciate.
quotes: You don’t need elaborate charts. You don’t need an incentive system. And you don’t need to beg, bribe, or threaten students to behave.
For the minute-by-minute reality of a working classroom, the best way to have more fun is…well…to have more fun.
Your students don’t have to be sweaty and crimson-faced to have a good time. You don’t have to make your classroom riotous and chaotic. And you don’t have to be knee-slapping funny .
Nothing I’ve ever done as a teacher has gotten more response from students or generated more fun, more mystery, more excitement, and more behavior-influencing rapport than telling a story.

You can’t have fun with your students if you don’t like them. Seeing the best in your students, enjoying who they are as people, and appreciating their sense of humor and unique personalities is a choice you make.
Students who are happy to be in your class, who like you, and who appreciate the organized, efficient, and fun classroom you’ve created, will jump through fire to pay you back.
